Alex — following our call this morning, I put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) focused purely on the environment activation items we agreed are blocking the first ingest tests. Goal is to get BrightWave a production-like sandbox in 2 weeks so we can run the evaluation suite.

High level asks (can you confirm owners + target dates?):
- Org & tenant creation: BrightWave SRE to provide tenant name and preferred org admin email. (Need by Apr 29)
- API keys: Redwood will issue ephemeral API keys for the POC; BrightWave to confirm whether you will use service account or short-lived keys. (Key ready by Apr 30)
- IP allowlist: provide the list of outbound IPs for ingestion and webhook callbacks. We need CIDR blocks and low/medium ports. (CSV by Apr 30)
- VPC peering: exchange peering YAML and schedule a 2-hour maintenance window for routing verification. (Peering window May 3–7)

I attached a one-page MAP_BrightWave_v1.pdf that maps owners and dates; Marissa is on the thread for technical details. If those dates look tight, flag the items you want to move first.

Next steps: please reply with the SRE contact for peering + procurement contact for MSA/terms. I’ll update the MAP and send a polished timeline.

Thanks,

Alex / Soojin — adding technical detail so Maya/eng@brightwave.com has what they need to start the peering work:

API keys and org setup (short summary)
- We can issue two modes of keys: (1) service-account long-lived keys scoped to the evaluation tenant, or (2) short-lived ephemeral keys issued by our token service (recommended for security). If BrightWave wants to generate its own keys, we support OIDC-connected service accounts — tell us which approach and we’ll send the setup steps.

IP allowlist
- Attached is ip-allowlist.csv with the minimal egress IP blocks for the POC and recommended ports (443, 80 for health checks, 5222 for internal agent comms if you enable the connector). If you have a strict NAT setup, we can map port-specific rules; otherwise provide the CIDR list and we’ll confirm.

VPC peering
- Attached: vpc-peer-template.yaml (sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippet and peering/route validation checklist). Typical flow:
  1) Exchange peering IDs and routing ranges.
  2) Create peering connections in your account and accept in ours.
  3) Run a 2-hour routing validation window (we'll coordinate traceroutes and token round trips).

Preferred peering validation windows: May 3rd 10:00–12:00 PDT or May 5th 14:00–16:00 PDT. Let us know which works for Maya and the SRE team.

I attached the three files referenced above. Happy to jump on a 30-min tech sync with Maya later today or tomorrow.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: vpc-peer-template.yaml (stub), ip-allowlist.csv (stub)
